slides.say: A B C D is a parallelogram, and E lies on A D. Given: A B is nine centimeters, A E is four centimeters, angle A B C is seventy-two degrees, and angle B C E is fifty-four degrees. What is the perimeter of the parallelogram, in centimeters?
at: A B C D is a parallelogram

slides.say: The perimeter is the sum of the four sides, A B plus B C plus C D plus A D. We know only one side, A B, and a piece of A D. [short pause] So we'll find the missing sides one at a time, with the rules of the parallelogram.

[short pause] In a parallelogram, opposite sides are parallel and equal. A B is nine, so C D is nine too. B C and A D are equal to each other, but we don't know them yet. We do know part of A D. A E is four, and that will probably help.
at: so C D is nine too

slides.say: Now the angles. Angle B is seventy-two. Opposite angles in a parallelogram are equal, so angle D is seventy-two too. Angles next to each other add up to one hundred eighty, so the whole angle C is one hundred eighty minus seventy-two, which is one hundred eight.
Angle B C E is fifty-four, so the rest of angle C, angle E C D, is one hundred eight minus fifty-four, which is fifty-four too. So C E cuts angle C into two equal halves. It's an angle bisector.
at: so the rest of angle C

slides.say: Now look at triangle E D C. Two of its angles are known, seventy-two at D and fifty-four at C. The angles of a triangle add up to one hundred eighty. Seventy-two plus fifty-four is one hundred twenty-six, and one hundred eighty minus one hundred twenty-six is fifty-four. So angle D E C is fifty-four.
at: So angle D E C is fifty-four

slides.say: There's also a shorter way to see it. E D is parallel to B C, so we get a Z, and the angles inside a Z are equal. So angle D E C equals angle B C E, fifty-four, right away.

In triangle E D C, the angles at E and at C are both fifty-four. Equal angles face equal sides, so the triangle is isosceles, and E D equals C D, which is nine. Remember this pattern. An angle bisector in a parallelogram cuts off an isosceles triangle.
at: and E D equals C D

slides.say: Almost done. All of A D is four plus nine, which is thirteen, and B C is thirteen too, because opposite sides are equal. The perimeter is nine plus thirteen plus nine plus thirteen. Nine and nine is eighteen, thirteen and thirteen is twenty-six, and together forty-four. Choice number three is our answer. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: All of A D is four plus nine
Choice number three is our answer
